name: Quiet Proposal Chase Queue
value_proposition: Turn a sent-proposal export into a skip-ruled silence queue with a written cadence and field-limited drafts — the owner reviews, edits, and sends from their own email, and the kit never sends or writes back.
persona: Owner or closer at a contractor, agency, or professional-services firm who sends 5-20 written quotes or proposals a month and loses more deals to silence than to a stated no.
problem: Sent proposals sit unopened. The team moves on to new requests, then notices a large quote went quiet only when the close date has passed.
workflow: 1. The person writes silence rules and cadence before any queue: silence-if-sent-before date (or days-of-silence threshold), owner minimum amount, statuses that are never chased (default declined, won, on-hold), and the follow-up cadence ladder (for example day 5-11 recap, day 12-20 check-in, day 21+ close-the-loop). PERSON DECIDES: the silence date, the minimum, the never-chase statuses, and the cadence steps.

2. The person exports sent proposals as CSV with proposal id, customer, amount, sent date, status, last inbound reply date, close date, and one line item, plus the export's as-of date. They open last week's outcome log. PERSON DECIDES: which columns to keep. Remove emails, phone numbers, and any columns the workflow does not need. This is an export review, not a live CRM, PandaDoc, DocuSign, email, or spreadsheet connection.

3. The person checks the data settings of their AI assistant (chat history, training use, and file retention) before pasting or uploading anything. File upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings. PERSON DECIDES: whether to paste the rows as text, upload a file, or not use AI for this data at all.
4. The person pastes the Silence Queue Prompt and their rules from the Silence Threshold and Cadence Worksheet, then attaches or pastes the export and the outcome log.

5. AI runs SKIP RULES FIRST. It sets aside declined, won, owner-marked on-hold, already followed up this period per the outcome log, sent dates on or after the silence-if-sent-before date, amounts below the owner's minimum, and rows missing proposal id or amount. Every skipped row is listed with its reason. PERSON DECIDES: whether a below-minimum or on-hold proposal should still be reviewed.

6. AI ranks remaining silent proposals by amount largest first, then by days since sent (oldest first when amounts tie). It assigns a cadence step from the owner's written ladder using days since sent as of the export as-of date. PERSON DECIDES: whether a queued row is actually worth chasing before any draft is used.

7. For each queued proposal, AI cites only export fields as CONFIRMED and drafts one follow-up using only proposal id, amount, sent date, and the one line item from the export. It does not invent an objection, a competitor, a discount, or a deadline the export does not contain. It labels CONFIRMED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. PERSON DECIDES: whether each recommended action happens.

8. The person uses the Follow-up Review Checklist and checks every CONFIRMED number against the export row. PERSON DECIDES: edit and send from their own email, hold, mark lost or declined, or do nothing. The Blueprint never sends and never writes a tracker field. Outcomes (replied, still silent, lost, declined, on hold) go in the outcome log and feed next week's run.
before: The owner remembers a couple of big quotes, sends one awkward bump, and the rest expire unnoticed.
after: Each week the owner reviews a silence queue with skip reasons, a cadence step that matches days since sent, and drafts whose numbers match the export. Last week's declined and on-hold rows stay out.

guided_demo.fictional_data_notice: All proposals, customer names, amounts, sent dates, statuses, and dates on this page are fictional. No real customer or proposal data is used, and nothing is connected to a CRM, PandaDoc, DocuSign, email, spreadsheet, or any other live system.

kit_contents.title: Silence Queue Setup Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Step-by-step setup for the weekly run. It covers writing the silence-if-sent-before date, owner minimum, never-chase statuses, and cadence ladder; exporting sent proposals as CSV with proposal id, customer, amount, sent date, status, last inbound, close date, one line item, and as-of date; removing emails and phone numbers; opening last week's outcome log; checking the AI tool's data settings before pasting or uploading; and the rule that this is an export review, not a live CRM, PandaDoc, or email connection. It notes that file upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings, and that rows can be pasted as text instead.

kit_contents.title: Silence Queue Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt that runs SKIP RULES FIRST, lists every skip with its reason, ranks remaining silent proposals by amount then by days since sent, assigns a cadence step from the owner's written ladder, drafts follow-ups using only proposal id, amount, sent date, and one line item, and labels CONFIRMED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. It forbids inventing an objection, competitor, discount, or deadline, sending email, and writing tracker fields.

kit_contents.title: Week-to-Week Outcome Log Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt for the following week. It reads the previous outcome log with the new export, skips rows whose log outcome is declined, lost, or on_hold, keeps still_silent and replied rows labelled from the log, and forbids sending or writing tracker fields.

kit_contents.title: Silence Threshold and Cadence Worksheet
kit_contents.purpose: Browser-only form where the person sets the silence-if-sent-before date, owner minimum amount, statuses that are never chased, and the three cadence buckets (recap, check-in, close-the-loop day ranges). It generates a copyable rules block to paste with the prompts. Nothing is saved to Atlas.

kit_contents.title: Outcome Log Template
kit_contents.purpose: Column layout (week_of, proposal, customer, amount, action_taken, outcome, notes) with allowed outcome values replied, still_silent, lost, declined, on_hold, skipped_too_recent, skipped_below_minimum, skipped_won, skipped_already_followed_up, and the fictional P-441 still_silent and P-430 declined rows from the guided demo. Includes a Copy CSV button so the person can start their own spreadsheet.

kit_contents.title: Follow-up Review Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Interactive, session-only checklist used before contacting anyone. It confirms that SKIP RULES FIRST ran, that every skip has a reason, that remaining rows are amount-ranked then by days since sent, that the cadence step matches the owner's ladder, that CONFIRMED amounts and dates match the export row, that labels are separate, that the draft uses only proposal id, amount, sent date, and line item, that no objection or deadline was invented, that silence was not treated as proof of interest or of a lost deal, and that the person will send from their own email.

kit_contents.title: Fictional Sample Proposal Export
kit_contents.purpose: The same fictional four-row proposal CSV used in the guided demo, labelled as fictional, with a Copy CSV button. The person can practice the full workflow in their AI tool before using real proposal data.

kit_contents.title: Data and Safety Guidance
kit_contents.purpose: Rules for handling proposal exports in AI tools: review data settings, remove emails and phone numbers, do not paste passwords or payment details, do not invent an objection, competitor, discount, or deadline, do not treat silence as proof of interest or of a lost deal, and do not chase proposals logged as declined, lost, or on-hold. It also states that file upload support differs by plan and that nothing is sent automatically.

decision_rules: Write SKIP RULES FIRST and apply it before ranking, cadence assignment, or drafting any follow-up.
Skip any row whose status is declined, won, or on-hold (or any status on the owner's never-chase list). Show the reason 'status <status>'.
Skip any row already followed up this period per the outcome log. Show the reason 'already followed up this period'.
Skip any row whose sent_date is on or after the owner's silence_if_sent_before date. Show the reason 'sent <date> is on or after your silence date <date>'.
Skip any row whose amount is below the owner's minimum. Show the reason 'amount $<amount> is below your $<minimum> minimum'.
Skip any row missing proposal id or amount. Show the reason 'missing proposal id or amount' under NEEDS YOUR CHECK, not in the queue.
Rank remaining silent proposals by amount, largest first. If two share an amount, older sent_date first.
Assign cadence from the owner's written ladder using days since sent as of as_of. Default ladder: 5-11 days recap; 12-20 days check-in; 21+ close-the-loop. Show which bucket matched.
Drafts may state only proposal id, amount, sent date, and the one line item from the export row. Do not invent an objection, competitor name, discount, urgency deadline, or contact email or phone.
Silence is CONFIRMED missing inbound reply in the export. It is not proof of interest and not proof the deal is lost. That caution is AI INTERPRETATION.
The draft is a draft only. Do not send it. Do not edit a CRM or proposal-tracker field. Suggest an outcome-log row; the person adds it.
On a later run, start from a new export and the current outcome log. Skip rows whose log outcome is declined, lost, or on_hold.
human_ai_boundary: AI applies skip rules and lists every skipped row with its reason. The person decides whether a below-minimum or on-hold proposal should still be reviewed.
AI ranks by amount and days since sent and assigns a cadence step from the owner's written ladder. The person decides whether a queued row is actually worth chasing.
AI drafts follow-ups using only export fields. The person checks every number against the export row, edits the wording, and approves it.
AI labels silence as neither a yes nor a no. The person decides whether to chase, hold, mark declined or lost, or do nothing.
AI never sends email and never writes a tracker or CRM field. The person sends from their own email, or decides not to.
AI reads the outcome log. Only the person records outcomes, and the log reflects what the person entered, not what AI assumed.
The person decides whether any recommended action happens.
safety: Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically. Every page states that the person sends it, and that nothing is sent automatically.
Atlas does not connect to a CRM, PandaDoc, DocuSign, email, spreadsheet, or any other vendor. It has no OAuth flow, no API call, and does not upload the person's data to any third party.

Before pasting or uploading exports to an AI tool, the person is told to review that tool's data settings (such as chat history, training use, and file retention) and to remove emails, phone numbers, and other columns the workflow does not need.
The kit tells the person not to paste account passwords, payment card numbers, or bank details into the AI tool.
File upload support and data controls in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini differ by plan, account, and admin settings. The kit says so and does not claim any plan includes a specific capability.

The kit tells the person not to invent an objection, competitor, discount, or deadline, not to treat silence as proof of interest or of a lost deal, and not to chase proposals logged as declined, lost, or on-hold.
All demo and sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional on the page.
Worksheet entries and checklist progress stay in the browser session only and are not saved to Atlas.
The pages contain no statistics, close-rate claims, savings, ROI claims, prices, or checkout. The only dollar figures are the fictional proposal amounts and the fictional $1,000 minimum.
required_data_tools: Proposal or quote tracker export (CSV) from a CRM, PandaDoc, or spreadsheet with proposal id, customer, amount, sent date, status, last inbound reply date, close date, and one line item
Owner-set silence threshold (silence_if_sent_before date), minimum amount, and follow-up cadence ladder
Outcome log spreadsheet, started from the kit's Outcome Log Template
The owner's own email client for any follow-up
A file-capable AI assistant. File upload support differs by plan, account, and admin settings; rows can be pasted as text instead.

constraints: Private preview only. The guided demo lives at /blueprints/ai-proposal-follow-up-assistant and the Premium kit at /blueprints/ai-proposal-follow-up-assistant/kit. Both pages set robots noindex and are not linked from the homepage, header navigation, or the sitemap.

The Premium kit requires requireUser from src/lib/auth.ts and hasActiveEntitlement for this product. It is labelled "Premium · Private preview". It shows no Stripe price, checkout, or Buy Premium unless the product is already in PAID_PRODUCTS.
All sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional. No live connector, OAuth flow, API call, or upload to a third party.
AI prepares; the person decides. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled separately. Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically.
No invented statistics, savings, or ROI claims. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini capabilities differ by plan; say so where it matters.

Product files live in app/blueprints/ai-proposal-follow-up-assistant/, components/premium/ai-proposal-follow-up-assistant/, and src/lib/premium/ai-proposal-follow-up-assistant/. Register the Blueprint in src/lib/blueprints.ts. Do not edit Daily Inbox, Collections product behavior, Stripe, or Production.
e2e/ai-proposal-follow-up-assistant/authenticated.spec.ts is read-only once it exists. Do not skip, weaken, or rewrite it. Authenticated QA uses automatic session refresh.
Keyboard accessible, visible labels, no horizontal scrolling at a phone-sized viewport, no console errors.
